shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Four vanilla-matched per-level sizes (126/190/250/300) and level counts are bought from a fixed 192,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Content on lower levels draws smaller once per level of drop, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** this body is a running spec, not a changelog. Sections 1-19 are the architecture; §20 is the third-party compat library; §21-22 are OPEN BUGS from the published build. Keep every ⚠ - each one cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~72 files, ~20,500 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text; keep it that way.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities in order: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather and settings passes are all VERIFIED IN PLAY.
UNVERIFIED IN PLAY: below-snow, the depth shrink (§6g), the new-game camera anchor (§8a), the whole §18 audit, the reroll grid (§6d-REROLL), all four §20 compat patches, and the new size tiers + preview Clamp fix (§2, §6d-CLAMP).

**⚠ THREE BUGS FROM THE PUBLISHED BUILD.**
1. Preview only worked at 190x190 - **DIAGNOSED AND FIXED** (§6d-CLAMP), unverified.
2. Fog/rocks appear to regenerate on save reload - **NOT DIAGNOSED, HELD** (§21).
3. With Geological Landforms installed, rivers show on the world map/preview but **never appear on the generated map** - **PARTLY DIAGNOSED, HELD** (§22).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, with a permanently-fogged gutter between them. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + MinGutter) / 64) * 64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position). Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 250 / 300.

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** The path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH map dimensions is distorted, and that bug class cannot appear on an ordinary square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, six shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river and lake centre; random/edge cell (§15a); VEE Crater jitter (§20) | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e); **VEE LoneIsland and Crater (§20)** | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); **GL landform grids (§20d, §22)** | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin measured off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b, §15d); **river WIDTH (§20)** | re-base onto the cell's own band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window AND reroll grid (§6d); **GL `TransformIntoMapSpace` (§22)** | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar**, one per-tick value for the whole map | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), **GL landform roof sweep (§20)** | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |

Classify a new bug into one of these six, but PROVE it. Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical implementation of the FIELD rewrite** (`z' = (z % Slot) + (Size.z - bandHeight)/2`) plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for consumers that sample a noise field directly. Extracted from the coast prefix at the THIRD consumer.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 192,000 cells

## ⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT ON BAND HEIGHT
`Slot = ceil((bandHeight + 2)/64)*64` must be 64-aligned; the band height only has to leave `MinGutter` rows under that boundary. The original tiers were all 64k-2 (126/190/254) - the *tightest* fit - and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**, which kept vanilla's own numbers off the list. 64k-2 is the CHEAPEST point, not the only legal one.

| size | slot | gutter | cells/band | playable | max levels | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 |
| 190 | 192 | 2 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 5 | 182,400 |
| **250** | 256 | 6 | 64,000 | 97.7% | 3 | **192,000** |
| **300** | 320 | 20 | 96,000 | 93.8% | 2 | **192,000** |

250 and 300 are vanilla's Medium and Large **exactly**. **The budget is tuned, not guessed:** 192,000 is simultaneously `3 x 64,000` and `2 x 96,000`, so both large tiers land dead on it, and `6 x 190`, `4 x 250`, `3 x 300` are all refused. Ladder 7/5/3/2, monotone, and **every tier still yields real z-levels** - which is why 350 (134,400/band) and 382 (146,688/band) are NOT offered: a second level costs more than the whole budget.

**⚠ 200 IS THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID.** Just PAST the 192 boundary: slot 256, gutter 56, 51,200 cells for 40,000 playable, 21.9% wasted - the worst point on the curve. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH, not a smooth function.** Recompute the table before adding any size.

**⚠ A WIDE GUTTER IS A FEATURE.** §14 records that "a spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" - the root of §15a and §4. The gutter is 6 rows at 250 and 20 at 300. Those cells were being rounded away to slot alignment regardless; this spends them on safety.

**Old saves are safe.** `bandHeight` is scribed per map and `SlotFor` is generic.

Per-level size is SQUARE, which is why `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` already yields a per-BAND count. Only `GenStep_AnimaTrees` and `GenStep_TerrainPatches` read `map.Area`. **Squareness is also a repair tool:** `Size.x == bandHeight`.

**⚠ The level chooser is also the lab.** `0 above / 0 below` generates an ORDINARY single-level map, the vanilla control. **STILL UNVERIFIED: does `0 up / 0 down` actually reach generation?**

**⚠ The chooser UI: own the widget, do not patch the data.** `Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play. Our radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly - **which is why `mapSize` is the authoritative record of the player's choice, and why nothing should re-derive it (§6d-CLAMP).** Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix; **adding a size tier means growing that number too** (now +288f).
**⚠ The chooser LATCHES global state, released in a `Finalizer`** (§18a).
**The level spinners are NOT known to be broken.** Run #190's "wrong plan" was USER ERROR. **The plan PERSISTS between colonies.**

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix, tick sweep, `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` BFSes the band graph; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop routing STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
`RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof: only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix normalises `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. Verified.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated drop. TEN systems share it. **EIGHT separate appearances of the single `- Slot` bug** (the eighth in the lighting overlay, written as INDEX arithmetic so the standing `grep '- Slot'` audit could not see it).

**`ABBands.TryResolveVisibleFrom` is now THE gate.** It folds the four-question preamble every caller was hand-rolling onto the descent, plus an optional unfogged check. Six passes are on it. Two legitimate exceptions: `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` needs the "in bounds but fogged" distinction for its air mask and fog fan, and the upward-shape consumers ask "is THIS thing what the column shows" and translate before descending.

Sun-shadow subtlety: its mask is neighbour-based, so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the smallest drop among the nine cells.
Still single-band AND unshrunk: the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw`.

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION (verified)
Four rejected attempts on record: force-linked wall masks, high-queue cover, wall-sprite suppression, and theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), one central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Check for ground before diagnosing anything about the top level.
Ore glyph bug: ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`, so a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole atlas sheet per cell.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS A SET OF MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` is a faithful port of vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Every OTHER vanilla pass that contributes to how ground looks needs its own mirror. Confirmed twice: **Water** (§6b) and **Snow** (§6f).
Mirrors: BelowV2 (terrain + things + fog fan), BelowLighting, BelowShadows, BelowEdgeShadows, BelowWatergen, BelowSnow, MountainCap.

**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS ALREADY HANDLED, AND KNOWING WHY MATTERS.** A foreign mod that injects geometry during `Thing.Print` prints into whatever `SectionLayer` is passed - including ours. It is nonetheless correct, because `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` brackets the call as `SnapshotVertCounts()` -> `t.Print(this)` -> `FinishNewVerts(drop, centre, shrink)`, and **`FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE, not by knowing which graphic emitted what**. Preserve that property.

**Cross-band invalidation: `Patch_MapDrawer_ABMirrorDirtyUp`, with an ASCENT RULE.** It mirrors dirty flags to bands above, so a new mirrored layer costs one `relevantChangeTypes` line. It used to climb to EVERY band unconditionally - the inverse of §5. The climb now stops at the first opaque floor, tested over the cell AND its eight neighbours. The FIRST step stays unconditional because `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` derives from exactly one Slot below. Also mirrors vanilla's `ProgramState != Playing` guard.

**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.** Seventeen layers rebuild per dirtied section, so an unbounded mirror multiplied every mined rock by bandCount. Steady-state fps never showed it; it lands in the hitches during mining and construction.

**⚠ SIX PASSES SHARE THE BELOW VIEW.** Any future per-frame geometry transform must be applied to ALL of them from one definition.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER: 1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect
`SectionLayer_Watergen` (vanilla, `internal`, cannot be subclassed) is `SectionLayer_Terrain` plus `waterDepthMaterial`, drawn to the WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's layer. The visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that texture at its own SCREEN position.
- Water missing from upper levels, FIXED: `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`.
- Rivers not generating, FIXED: remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`, which consumes it immediately). `GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first.
- **River WIDTH is now clamped too** (§20b). The centre was remapped years before the extent measured off it was.
- **⚠ ALL THREE OF THOSE PATCHES ARE DEAD WHEN GEOLOGICAL LANDFORMS IS INSTALLED. See §22.**

# 6b-LAKE. CLOSED: surface streaking accepted as vanilla appearance
PROVEN in run #173: a tile with water but no water mutators still streaked. **The ghost-river theory is dead.** Found en route: vanilla's flow builder ends `zero /= (float)num3` with no zero guard, writing NaN into a bilinear-filtered texture.

# 6c. DUBS MINT MINIMAP (verified)
ONE RECT, not seven patches. `DrawTextureFitted` preserves the TEXTURE's aspect, so use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`. Reflection only.

# 6d. MAP PREVIEW (m00nl1ght.MapPreview)
Never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap` - it builds a bare Map and runs a short genstep list on a background thread, so our banding prefix never fires. **Generate at the full stacked height and crop via `TexCoords`.** `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500, a stack reaches 896).

## 6d-CLAMP. ⚠ THE PUBLISHED BUG: PREVIEW ONLY WORKED AT 190x190 (FIXED, unverified)
`MapPreviewCompat.Stacked()` ran the incoming size through `ABMapSizeLimit.Clamp()`. **`Clamp` is not an identity snap** - it returns *the largest offered size ≤ input that fits at the current level count*. Map Preview passes **VANILLA's** configured size (250 by default), not our per-level pick:
```
Clamp(250) at 4 levels -> 254 excluded (>250), 190 fits -> 190
lastBandHeight = 190
TryBandRows(stackedZ): BandCount * SlotFor(190) == stackedZ ?
   player chose 190 -> true  -> crop works
   anything else    -> false -> "not one of ours" -> no crop, broken
```
The preview generated a 190-based stack **regardless of selection**.
**Fix: `ABMapSizeLimit.PlannedSize`.** `Clamp` answers "sanitise this number DOWN to something affordable" - correct for scenario/stale-config values and LOSSY by design. It was answering a different question: "what did the player choose?" That was never a derivation problem - the chooser writes `GameInitData.mapSize` directly, so it is on record.
Fixed alongside: `Stacked` clamped x and z INDEPENDENTLY though a band is square; `FixWindowAspect` re-Clamped `lastBandHeight`.

**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES, AND GL BUNDLES ONE.** `MapPreview.dll` (engine) is bundled by BOTH, byte-identical. But `MapPreviewWindow` and `MapSeedRerollWindow` live ONLY in `MapPreviewMod.dll`, which GL does not ship. **With GL installed and Map Preview NOT installed, `MapPreviewCompat.Active` is TRUE while the window types are ABSENT.** Correct today only because every target is null-guarded independently. **Do not "simplify" `Active` into a single gate.**

## 6d-REROLL. THE SEED REROLL GRID (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
**The seed needs NOTHING from us** - preview and committed map share the same store, and we only change SIZE.
**⚠ The window opened COMPLETELY EMPTY.** `UpdateElementSize` shapes each thumbnail as `y = width / mapSize.x * mapSize.z`:
```
126x896 stack, 2560px window, 6 per row
  elementSize.y = 403 / 126 * 896 = 2,866 px   (a 7:1 sliver)
  gridSize.y    = floor(1330 / 2886) = 0
  DesiredCount  = 0  ->  trim loop disposes every element
  TryAddElement -> `if (_elements.Count >= DesiredCount) return;` -> 0 >= 0 -> returns
```
**The SECOND consumer of the stacked size caught out by it.** Fixed by a postfix on `UpdateElementSize` re-deriving `_elementSize.y` from the BAND height, recomputing `_gridSize.y`, and kicking `TryAddElement` once. A POSTFIX repairing two statics, not a reimplementation.
- **Rejected: suppressing our inflation while the window is open** - every thumbnail would picture a map that will never generate.
- **Cropping is free:** the existing crop patch trims each thumbnail.
- **Accepted cost:** ~27 MB transient, 6/7 cropped away.

# 6e. COASTS (verified)
CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight)/2`, NO SCALING - stretching band-local z skews any non-axis-aligned field and makes displacement noise anisotropic.
**⚠ "Nine coastal mutators, none override `GetNoiseValue`" is about VANILLA ONLY.** VEE's LoneIsland family declares its own and drowns the colony (§20).

# 6f. BELOW-SNOW (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
**No mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed**, so below-snow was never emitted.
**The near-miss that hid it:** `CellTerrainAt` genuinely samples `map.snowGrid.GetDepth(below)`, but that value is consumed only by `MaterialFor`, to pick the POLLUTED variant. The right value read for an entirely different purpose.
Details: geometry built once and reused (NOT `ClearSubMeshes(All)`); iteration order must match `MakeBaseGeometry` (x outer, z inner, nine per cell); cells with nothing below still emit nine transparent vertices; all nine kernel samples taken at the CENTRE cell's drop.
**⚠ Open risk:** draw ordering is queue-decided. `MatBases.Snow` may need queue work.

# 6g. DEPTH SHRINK (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
The exponent is the accumulated drop (three levels down draws at 61%). Baked into vertices at print time. DEFAULT ON, slider 60-100%.
- **Printed things:** `FinishNewVerts` shrinks about `TrueCenter` and translates by `drop` in ONE pass, scale first. Operates on a VERTEX RANGE (§6a).
- **Live pawns:** right-multiply `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. Right-multiply is load-bearing; a left multiply slides every below pawn towards the map origin.
- **⚠ The atlas trap:** past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit that ignores `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. `Patch_PawnRenderer_ABBelowDisableCache` forces `disableCache` for below pawns only. **Verification must cross that boundary in both directions.**
- **⚠ V1's exclusion filter kept verbatim:** LINKED graphics print one quad per cell; natural rock excluded BY DEF (`mineable`/`isNaturalRock`) not by link type, because Better Mountains swaps rock to non-linked `Graphic_Random` wholesale.
- **Not tinted.** `SectionLayer_ABBelowLighting` already shades below content.
- **ReGrowth does NOT contest this.** Its transpiler targets `Graphic_Linked.Print` + 3 subclasses only, no-op unless `printingSnow`. Our filter already skips linked graphics.

**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add it as polish.** It worked and was cheap. Cut because the shrink alone carried the depth read, and perspective bought a second cue at the price of a real artifact. Re-opening needs a NEW reason and must re-solve the six-pass coupling.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Ore `x(1 + 0.45*(depth-1))`, cave openness `x(1 + 0.35*(depth-1))`, applied AFTER the settings clamp. **The ore multiplier scales `basementOreDensity` through our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`** - NOT vanilla's `countPer10kCellsRange`.
**⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.** Dead for months behind a confident, wrong sentence.
**Climate defaults:** +1 = -7, +2 = -16, +3 = -35, basement flat -6, wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50. **No ceiling clamp by design.**

# 8. CAMERA
`ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by LEVEL, not band index. `panMargin` 63.5 on every level.
**The clamp and the level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`.** Both on per-frame / per-GUI-event paths, exactly where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into an unplayable game. If the clamp trips, band switching stops too.

# 8a. NEW-GAME CAMERA ANCHOR (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
On a banded map two things move the colony AFTER `PlayerStartSpot` is chosen: `RescueStrandedColonists` and the carve.
**Confirmed in run #200:** `DropThingsNear failed to find a place to drop Nyx near (153, 0, 24).`
Fixed upstream (`FixPlayerStartSpot` prefers the colony's ACTUAL position) and as a backstop (`ABGameComp.StartedNewGame`). **⚠ That hook, and only that hook, runs after vanilla's own camera jump.**
**⚠ OPEN:** `z=24` was EXACTLY the `PodScatterMargin`. Vanilla's own pick landing there and my clamp pinning it there look IDENTICAL from outside.

# 9. GENERATION COST

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
`ABGenProfile.Report` prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, a `SCOPING:` toggle line, and two censuses. It caught a changed tile on its FIRST use. Emitted at WARNING level deliberately.

## 9b. ⚠ THE COST IS DESTRUCTION, NOT GENERATION
Run #188: gensteps 3,972 ms, carve 20,447 ms, 74,584 things destroyed. Generation 16%, destruction 84%. Per-destroy price is stable, so **op count is the only lever**. Mechanism is `ListerThings` removal, a linear `List.Remove` over ~100k-item lists.
**CLOSED:** carving before `FinalizeInit` is worth at most 169 ms of 24,600.

## 9c. The culprit was rock, proven by census
Run #190: 43,517 rock SUPPRESSED vs 4,939 DESTROYED of which only 238 rock. Stable across four tiles and three biomes.

## 9d. SHIPPED: `ABDoomedBands.cs`
Suppresses `GenSpawn.Spawn(ThingDef,...)` inside `GenStep_RocksFromGrid` for doomed SKY band cells. Safe because: **shape**, **state-neutrality**, **sky only**. Patched on the `ThingDef` overload so the cancel precedes `ThingMaker.MakeThing`.

## 9e. Run #196: the basement is the whole cost
FillRock bands 0-2 = 2,606 ms (82% of carve); Sky clear = 301 ms (9%).
**⚠ MY OWN §9d CAUTION IS FALSIFIED.** The basement `FillRock` keep hits only **14.4%** of the time. Suppressing trades 7,113 destroys (~1.4 s) for 6,873 extra spawns (~200 ms). **Net ~1.2 s.**
**Sign flip, a confirmation not a bug:** with rock suppressed, `Sky clear` per band INVERTED. Rock tapers upward, so higher bands have more OPEN ground, and chunks only grow on open ground.

## 9f. Post-audit numbers (#205-#207)
7-band total ~5.5 s -> **~4.1 s**; ms per destroy 0.325 -> 0.243.
**⚠ NOT PROVEN, confound stated:** every comparison crosses tiles and biomes. The plausible mechanism is the mirror `ProgramState` guard, not the `ScatterOres` allocation fix (~190 KB/band is worth a millisecond, not 695).
**⚠ THE NEW TIERS INVALIDATE EVERY ABSOLUTE TIMING ABOVE.** A 3 x 250 colony is 192,000 cells against 7 x 126's 112,896 - 1.7x. Re-baseline before comparing across the tier change.

## 9g. Next targets, ranked
1. **Basement rock suppression** (§9e), ~1.2 s.
2. **`GenStep_RockChunks`**, dominant survivor on sky-only maps.
3. **Scattered ruins, also a CONTENT BUG.** Count sized for ONE band, placement spans the stack, so **the surface loses a large share of the ruins vanilla intended**.
4. **`ABRockGen.PickIndex` evaluates every rock type's 6-octave Perlin per cell.** NOT DONE: changes generation determinism.

# 10, 11. PERF
59.6 fps at 96 pawns, mod ~2% of frame. **⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING.** Cost is concentrated in section-regeneration BURSTS. Any perf claim needs a mining/construction test with a multi-level plan, watching the frame graph.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
Band info, below layer/pawn reports, water report, transit health, stuck probe, lighting/shader/biome reports, bisect toggles, ABGenProfile, camera calibration.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST in the pinned palette across runs.** Run #172 opened with a stale `belowWater=False` that mimicked a fixed bug exactly. Now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE.
**⚠ Poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts.** Single-occurrence `[RimWorld]` warnings are filtered from summaries.
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always loses its LAST entry.** `EnsureAllNodesValid` walks BACKWARDS while `GetNode` is still lazily building the graph. Confirmed at n=3. Pad with a DISTINCT throwaway entry.
`AB2: band info` is the fastest ground truth for "what did this map actually generate as".

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **§21 fog/rocks on reload** - run the two-question observation.
2. **§22 GL rivers** - finish the diagnosis (read `TransformIntoMapSpace`).
3. **Verify the new tiers** (§2) and **the preview Clamp fix** - test all four sizes, not just 190.
4. **Verify the §18 audit**, the §20 compat patches (§20e), the reroll grid, depth shrink, camera anchor, below-snow.
5. **Basement rock suppression**; §9g items 3 and 4; audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators.
6. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, basement PATHING and wormholes, cavern basement (§18e).
7. **Below-pawn drawing is serial and cache-disabled.** Realtime-things pass single-band AND unshrunk.
8. **`ShotReport` cross-band accuracy silently drops target size.**
9. **Biomes! remains the least-understood neighbour** (40%).
10. **Store page still says three levels.**

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. A documented rejection may be re-opened only by naming the confound. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. An exact number is a diagnosis. A beautiful fit is not evidence. Knowing when to stop is a result.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed.** Generation 16%, deletion 84%.
**⚠ A census beats a magnitude.** "74,584 things" is not a diagnosis; "43,517 Granite and Limestone" is.
**⚠ Stamp the experiment's conditions into its own output.** The tile stamp voided four bad comparisons.
**⚠ Evidence consistent with both hypotheses is not evidence; the discriminating experiment is usually cheap.** The persisted spinner. The `z=24` start spot. The palette pin. And §21, where one click separates data from rendering.
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM SET IS ITSELF EVIDENCE - ASK WHAT THE AFFECTED THINGS SHARE.** In §21 the report named fog AND rocks and nothing else. Those are precisely the two things RimWorld stores as flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area` (`FogGrid.ExposeData` -> `LookBitArray(..., map.Area, ...)`; `MapFileCompressor` -> `MapSerializeUtility.LoadUshort`). Everything else - pawns, furniture, player-built walls - is saved individually. **When a bug report lists an odd pair, look for the storage mechanism they have in common before looking for a culprit mod.**
**⚠ An optimisation you declined for a stated reason still owes you the number.** The basement keep hit rate was 14.4% and the decision inverted.
**⚠ When a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes.**
**⚠ A correct value read for the wrong purpose looks like coverage.** Grep for the value's CONSUMER, not just its read site.
**⚠ A deleted feature's exclusion list is the expensive part.**
**⚠ Two cues for one property is one cue too many.**
**⚠ When two hooks both "run at startup", find the one that runs after the thing you are fixing.**
**⚠ Aim at the fact, not at the record of the intent.** `PlayerStartSpot` is a plan; the pawns are where the colony IS. **And `GameInitData.mapSize` IS the player's choice.**
**⚠ A LOSSY NORMALISER IS NOT A WAY TO READ A CHOICE.** `Clamp` was correct at its own job and completely wrong as an answer to "what did the user pick?" **When a function's contract is "snap to something valid", it can never RECOVER a value.** Ask whether the answer is already recorded before computing it.
**⚠ A CONSTRAINT SATISFIED BY EVERY EXAMPLE IS NOT NECESSARILY THE CONSTRAINT.** All three original sizes were 64k-2, read for months as "band height must be 64k-2". The real rule was only that *Slot* is 64-aligned. It cost vanilla-matched sizes until someone asked "what if we bump the size slightly?" **Derive the constraint from the mechanism, not from the set of things you already built.**
**⚠ A rule enforced by grepping for a SYNTAX only catches that syntax.**
**⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** The coast rewrite was extracted at the THIRD consumer, not the eighth.
**⚠ A comment is not an invariant.** **⚠ A kill switch with no call site is noise.** **⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.**
**⚠ The second consumer of a value you reshaped will not announce itself.**
**⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return, not slow code.**
**⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.**
**⚠ A finding scoped to vanilla does not transfer to mods, even when the sentence sounds general.** Re-state the scope INSIDE the finding.
**⚠ A SHARED METHOD NAME IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A CONFLICT.** The §20 audit flagged six collisions from names; reading the bodies cleared THREE. **False-positive rate on name-matching alone was 50%.** ReGrowth alone has now been cleared FOUR separate times.
**⚠ THE REAL CONFLICT IS USUALLY A REPLACEMENT, NOT A COLLISION.** Every §20 candidate was "we both patch X". The bug that actually shipped broken (§22) is the opposite shape: GL *substitutes its own worker for vanilla's*, so our patches do not fight it - **they simply never run**. A patch that is silently never invoked produces no error, no log line and no conflict warning. **When auditing a mod, ask what it REPLACES, not only what it patches.**
**⚠ Compat work is mostly deletion.** The deliverable from a 150-mutator mod was 2 patches. Find the inheritance edge before counting the defs.
**⚠ Design for the foreign patch you have not met.** `FinishNewVerts` transforms a VERTEX RANGE rather than a known graphic.
**⚠ Waste is often a sawtooth, not a curve.** Tabulate before choosing a number.
**⚠ The thing you rounded away may be load-bearing.** Wide gutters looked like pure waste and are the cheapest defence against the seam-crossing bug class.
**Claims versus facts.** A comment asserting why something is safe to delete is a claim (§7). Re-measure the assumption you are about to build on.
**Shapes.** Classify into one of the six. A slice of a tall map is not a short map. A uniform symptom is a scale or constant, a patchy one is data. An odd/even symptom is arithmetic.
**Patching.** When N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through - and when there is none, **wrap the DATA instead of the reader**. Patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it. Own the widget instead of patching the data it reads. Never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature - type `__instance` as `object`. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **State taken in a Prefix is released in a Finalizer, never a Postfix.** **Mirror the guard of the method you postfix.** **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing its body.** **Never clamp a Def field to fix one map.** **Prefer a foreign mod's published ExtensionPoint over racing its internals** (§22).
**Engine facts.** `TerrainDef.holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Draw order is settled by material render QUEUE, not altitude. Vanilla divides by a count without guarding zero. A spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter. `Banded` is FALSE for the whole of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses are auto-discovered on EVERY map. Any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`. Statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak; use a CWT. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread - latches taken during generation must be `[ThreadStatic]`. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. `CameraJumper.TryJump` and `MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` both silently return unless `ProgramState == Playing`. Humanlike pawns past `ZoomRootSize` 18 render from an atlas blit that ignores `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED, which is why the same work costs ~40x after `FinalizeInit`.** Harmony skips POSTFIXES when the original throws, but always runs FINALIZERS. **A prefix returning false skips the original but POSTFIXES STILL RUN.** **Harmony composes a prefix and a transpiler on the same method without conflict.** **`FogGrid` and compressible things (natural rock) are stored as flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`; everything else is saved individually.** **TileMutatorDefs compete within a `categories` entry, so a mod can REPLACE a vanilla mutator by declaring its own in the same category.**

# 21. ⚠ OPEN: FOG AND ROCKS ON SAVE RELOAD (HELD, NOT DIAGNOSED)
Reported from the published build: fog and rocks appear to regenerate after a save/load cycle.

**ELIMINATED** (each checked in source):
- `ABV2.*` settings-vs-map leakage - properly confined to generation and preview; every runtime consumer uses the map's scribed `ABBandMap`.
- Save compressibility - `IsSaveCompressible` records what is present; it cannot invent rock.
- Unsupported-roof collapse over carved sky bands - sky roofs ARE cleared.
- Stale `RebindAfterLoad` ordering - runs FIRST and unconditionally.
- **ReGrowth** - its two save-path patches are space-rock-only.
- **Alpha Biomes / Biomes! Core** - neither has any hook near the save path (no `MapFileCompressor`, no `CompressibilityDecider`, no `fogGrid`). Weak candidates.

**⚠ THE SYMPTOM PAIR IS THE STRONGEST CLUE, AND IT POINTS AT US.** Fog and natural rock are precisely the two things RimWorld stores as **flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`**:
```
FogGrid.ExposeData  -> DataExposeUtility.LookBitArray(ref fogGrid, map.Area, "fogGrid")
MapFileCompressor   -> MapSerializeUtility.LoadUshort(compressedData, map, ...)
                       -> ThingMaker.MakeThing(def); thing.SetPositionDirect(c)
```
Everything else - pawns, furniture, stockpiles, **player-built walls** - is saved individually. (Player walls are explicitly excluded from compression: `IsSaveCompressible` rejects `Building { canChangeTerrainOnDestroyed: false }`; natural rock leaves rough stone so it stays compressible.) **The reported pair is exactly the set that would break if a per-cell array desynced, and nothing else would.** We are the mod that makes `map.Area` an unusual shape.

**Three live hypotheses:** (a) real data, something re-runs generation-like work on load; (b) rendering, the below-view layers redraw recomputed state; (c) per-cell array desync on the save/load round trip.

**⚠ THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION - ONE LOAD, TWO QUESTIONS:**
1. **Click a reappeared rock.** Selectable/mineable -> real data. Not selectable -> rendering, (b).
2. **Check a player-built wall or stockpile in the same area.** Intact -> (c), per-cell arrays desynced while individually-saved things are fine. Also disturbed -> (a), something re-ran generation.

Do not write a fix before this; the hypotheses predict identical screenshots and completely different fixes.
**Also worth knowing before any bisect: did it reproduce on a light modlist?** If yes, the mod theory dies outright.

# 22. ⚠ CONFIRMED: GEOLOGICAL LANDFORMS SUPPRESSES RIVERS (HELD, PARTLY DIAGNOSED)
Reported and confirmed: with GL installed, a river tile shows a river on the world map and in the preview, but **the generated map has no river**.

## What is established
**GL REPLACES vanilla river generation outright - it does not patch it.** `GL_River`, `GL_RiverConfluence`, `GL_RiverDelta`, `GL_RiverIsland`, `GL_RiverSource` and `GL_RiverTerrain` are `TileMutatorDef`s in the **`River` category** built on `TileMutatorWorker_Landform`, not on `TileMutatorWorker_River`. Mutators compete within a category, so GL's win and vanilla's worker never runs.

**Consequence: every river patch we own is on a dead path when GL is installed** - §6b `GetRiverCenter`, §6b `GetLakeCenter`, and §20b's width clamp. They do not conflict with GL; **they are simply never invoked**, which is why this produced no error and no log line.

**GL's river comes from a completely different pipeline:**
```
Landform.OutputWaterFlow.GetRiverTerrain()
  -> Landform.TransformIntoMapSpace(...)
  -> ApplyBuffered(map.Size, TerrainAt, SetTerrain)      // terrain
  -> ApplyWaterFlow(map)                                  // waterInfo.riverFlowMap
```
`TransformIntoMapSpace` is the §20d open item: landform grids are built in node space and mapped onto the map using its dimensions, so on a 126x896 map a square landform is stretched 7:1 down the column. That is the ASPECT RATIO row of the slicing rule.

**A detail that may explain the preview/actual split:** `ApplyWaterFlow` is explicitly SKIPPED during preview (`if (!MapPreviewAPI.IsGeneratingPreview)`) while the river TERRAIN is applied in both. So preview and real map run different amounts of this pipeline.

## What is NOT established
- The exact behaviour of `Landform.TransformIntoMapSpace` and `MapSpaceToNodeSpaceFactor`. **Read these before writing anything.** Whether the river misses the surface band entirely, or is drawn and then lost, is not yet proven.
- Whether our carve interacts (it runs as a `GenerateContentsIntoMap` POSTFIX, after GL's mutators).
- `ApplyWaterFlow` indexes as `i * map.Size.z + j` (x-major). Vanilla's `riverFlowMap` convention needs checking against this; on a square map a transposed index is invisible, on a 7:1 map it is not. **Unverified, and a promising thread.**

## The fix surface
**`GeologicalLandformsAPI` publishes `ExtensionPoint<IntVec2, int> LandformGridSize` (default 250)** - a sanctioned hook mapping map size to landform grid size, and GL maintains `ModCompat_` classes for MapReroll, MapDesigner, PrepareLanding, RocketMan and others. **We should be one of those, not a mod fighting its internals.** Note the extension point sets RESOLUTION, which may not by itself correct the 7:1 stretch; that likely needs `TransformIntoMapSpace` fed a band rect.

## Interim
Until fixed, GL + a river tile is a known-bad combination. **§20e's river-width test must run with GL DISABLED**, or it tests a code path that never executes.
